title: Zur Theorie der Potenzreste
notes: Monatshefte fur Mathematik und Physik 3 (1892) 265-284. For coprime a > b >= 1, a^n - b^n has a prime divisor dividing no earlier term, with the finitely many stated exceptions. The base-2 case is earlier and is Bang 1886 (Tidsskrift for Mathematik): 2^n - 1 has a primitive prime divisor for every n except n = 1 and n = 6. Neither original was read here; both statements are standard. USED HERE FOR TWO THINGS, both recorded at docs/problems/juggler_mersenne_floor_power.md. (a) The cyclotomic factorisation 2^n - 1 = prod over d | n of Phi_d(2) has Phi_2(2) = Phi_6(2) = 3, the unique collision in the range, and that single coincidence simultaneously kills the primitive divisor at n = 6 -- Bang's only composite exception -- and creates the square in M_6 = 1 * 3 * 7 * 3 = 63 = 3^2 * 7. So the laboratory's squarefreeness witness at a = 6 is the named exceptional index rather than an arbitrary composite. (b) THE NEGATIVE USE, which is the one that matters for the cycle problem: Bang and Zsigmondy govern a^n - b^n with ONE moving exponent, while the cycle gap 3^o - 2^K has two independently moving exponents and is not a Cunningham number. That is the precise reason classical primitive-divisor theory does not reach the gap, where the laboratory previously recorded only the observation that it does not. Results on a^m - b^n with both exponents free (Bugeaud, Luca and others) are a different and much weaker body of work and no gap constraint is claimed from them here.
